# Overview

This page describes the
**beta-binomial** extension, which models the extra cell-line-to-cell-line
variance directly rather than assuming pure binomial sampling noise.

Sites tested: the same **5-fold union (≥ 1 fold)** set,
**`r format(12416, big.mark=",")` sites**. Samples: the same **50 genotyped
cell lines**. Covariates: the same **M-value PCs** (below).

# The model

For a given pU site, let individual $i$ have $y_i$ converted reads out of
$n_i$ total reads, but now allow the modification rate itself to vary around
its mean $\mu_i$ (a Beta-distributed mixing probability):

$$
p_i \sim \text{Beta}(\alpha_i, \beta_i), \qquad y_i \mid p_i \sim \text{Binomial}(n_i, p_i)
$$
$$
\text{logit}(\mu_i) = \beta_0 + \beta_g G_i + z_i^\top\gamma, \qquad
\mu_i = \frac{\alpha_i}{\alpha_i+\beta_i}, \qquad
\phi = \frac{1}{\alpha_i+\beta_i+1}
$$

Marginalizing over $p_i$ gives the **beta-binomial** distribution for $y_i$,
with the same mean model as the binomial but a different variance:

$$
\text{Var}(y_i) = n_i\mu_i(1-\mu_i)\big[\,1+(n_i-1)\phi\,\big]
$$

- $\phi \in [0,1)$ — the **overdispersion / intra-class-correlation**
  parameter: how much the $n_i$ reads at one cell line behave like correlated
  (not independent) trials. $\phi=0$ recovers the binomial exactly.
- The bracketed term $1+(n_i-1)\phi$ is a **variance inflation factor** — the
  same form as the design effect in clustered/survey data. It grows with
  depth $n_i$, so high-depth cell lines are *not* automatically down-weighted
  as much as the binomial would assume, once $\phi>0$.
- One $\phi$ per site (not per cell line, not per SNP) — a single dispersion
  shared across the site's 50 observations.

# QTL mapping: the beta-binomial score test

Testing $\beta_g$ per (site, cis-SNP) pair the same way as the binomial (an
LRT refit per SNP) would require re-fitting the beta-binomial's joint MLE for
every cis-SNP — far too slow to permute (~200,000 CPU-hours for the full
scan; see the [score-vs-LRT page](qtl_mapping_score_vs_lrt.html) for the
arithmetic). Instead we use a **Rao score test**: fit the null once per site,
then test every cis-SNP via a fast vectorized computation.

The null model is fit by maximum likelihood ($\beta_0,\gamma,\phi$ jointly).
The score test then needs the **exact** score and (observed) information of
the beta-binomial log-likelihood at that null fit — closed form via digamma
($\psi$) and trigamma ($\psi'$) functions. With $k=(1-\phi)/\phi$,
$a_i=\mu_ik$, $b_i=(1-\mu_i)k$ (so $a_i+b_i=k$ is constant in $\mu_i$, which
is what keeps this tractable):

$$
r_i = k\,\big[\psi(y_i{+}a_i)-\psi(a_i)-\psi(n_i{-}y_i{+}b_i)+\psi(b_i)\big]\,\mu_i(1-\mu_i)
$$
$$
w_i = -k^2\big[\psi'(y_i{+}a_i)-\psi'(a_i)+\psi'(n_i{-}y_i{+}b_i)-\psi'(b_i)\big]\big(\mu_i(1-\mu_i)\big)^2
      - r_i\,(1-2\mu_i)
$$
$$
U = G^\top r, \qquad V = G^\top\!\text{diag}(w)\,G - (\cdots),
\qquad U^2/V \sim \chi^2_1
$$

As $\phi\to0$ ($k\to\infty$) this reduces exactly to the binomial's
$r_i=y_i-n_i\mu_i$, $w_i=n_i\mu_i(1-\mu_i)$ — the beta-binomial score is a
generalization of the exact binomial case, not an independent approximation.
Validated against a numerical gradient/Hessian of the true log-likelihood
(exact match) and against the real LRT (rank correlation **0.955** on real
sites, unbiased — matching the binomial's own exactness). Detail and live
validation: [score-vs-LRT page](qtl_mapping_score_vs_lrt.html).

```r
nf  <- fit_null_betabin(y, n, X)      # phi estimated once (the slow joint MLE)
p_snp <- score_pvals(nf, G)           # per cis-SNP, exact score/info, same engine as the binomial
```

# Significance

Same three-step procedure as the binomial model.

## 1. Permutation as a calibration check

Same audit as the binomial: permute the phenotype across the 50 cell lines
(5 seeds), refit **fresh** (phi re-estimated under each permutation), collect
nominal p-values, check $\lambda\approx1$.

**Result** (5kb, 3 PCs): permuted-null $\lambda\approx$**1.13** (range
1.07-1.22 across 5 seeds) — close to the ideal 1, and well below the
binomial's ~3.4. Real data $\lambda=2.37$. See the [results
page](qtl_mapping_summary_betabinomial.html#calibration) for the table and
QQ-plot.

## 2. Within-site correction (permutation beta-approximation)

Same procedure as the binomial: minimum nominal p across a site's cis-SNPs,
permutation null of that minimum (1000x), Beta(a,b) fit, adjusted per-site p
from the Beta CDF.

**Where $\phi$ is held fixed**: this step alone needs 1000 permutations *per
site*, so refitting the full joint MLE ($\beta_0,\gamma,\phi$) for every one
would be far too slow. Since the score test treats $\phi$ as a fixed nuisance
parameter, $\phi$ is **estimated once per site** (the slow joint MLE above),
then held fixed across all 1000 permutations — each permutation only refits
the **mean**, a plain **weighted binomial GLM** on $y/n$ with prior weights
$n_i/c_i$ (this solves the beta-binomial mean equation exactly for fixed
$\phi$):

```r
nf_full <- fit_null_betabin(y, n, X)          # slow: estimate phi (once per site)
phi <- nf_full$phi
# fast: refit only the mean, phi fixed -- reused for all 1000 permutations
nf_perm <- bb_score_setup(y_perm, n_perm, X, phi)
```

This is ~13x faster than a full refit (~1ms vs. ~13ms). It is not a perfect
substitute for freely re-estimating $\phi$ (fixed-$\phi$ and free-$\phi$
exact scores agree with rank correlation 0.978 on real sites, not 1.0), but
what matters for validity is that the **same** fixed-$\phi$ procedure is
applied identically to the observed data and to every permutation, so a
systematic bias should largely cancel in the resulting permutation p-value —
confirmed by the calibration check above ($\lambda\approx1.13$).

**Note**: the calibration check in step 1 does *not* use this fixed-$\phi$
shortcut — it re-estimates $\phi$ fresh for every permutation, since it is
specifically auditing whether the fitting procedure itself is unbiased.

## 3. Across-site correction

BH-FDR (and q-values) over the per-site adjusted p, same as the binomial.

# Model fit across PC counts

The joint MLE ($k$ PCs + intercept + $\phi$) is reliably fittable across the
full swept range, $k\in\{3,...,20\}$: ~7,600 of 12,416 sites fit at k=20 (vs.
the binomial's ~7,900 at the same k). See the [results
page](qtl_mapping_summary_betabinomial.html) for the sites-fit table.

# Data

- **Sites**: 5-fold union, ≥ 1 fold — `r format(12416, big.mark=",")` pU sites.
- **Phenotype**: per site, per cell line — converted reads $C$ ($=y$) out of
  total depth $N$ ($=C+T$), identical to the binomial model (no
  transformation).
- **Genotypes**: cis SNPs within a window of each site (±5/20/50/100kb),
  common variants (MAF≥0.05) from the 50 cell lines' genotypes.
- **Covariates $z$**: M-value phenotype PCs — identical construction to the
  [binomial model](qtl_mapping_binomial_model.html#Covariates:_M-value_phenotype_PCs)
  (site-specific $(\pi_s, 1-\pi_s)$ pseudocount), swept over
  $k \in \{3,5,7,10,15,20\}$ (reliably fittable across the full range).
